title: Avatar Workshop (1 class)
summary: Give a voice agent a face, built with Pipecat. Learn why businesses use avatars, try one in the browser, then build your own Pipecat bot: Deepgram Flux listens and speaks, Claude thinks and SpatialReal animates a photoreal face. Leave able to turn it into a front-desk assistant, tutor or anything else.
detail: Everyone sits down, adds their own keys and talks to a live avatar in the browser: it interviews them for a couple of minutes, so they feel how an avatar looks, sounds and keeps up. The SpatialReal team then presents their product and pricing. The main part builds the same avatar as a Pipecat pipeline on each laptop, with a guided tour of bot.py: frames, processors, the pipeline order, memory and events. The last part turns it into a business assistant using one setting and a text file.
outcome: Your own Pipecat avatar bot running on your laptop, an understanding of how a Pipecat pipeline fits together, and a front-desk version you can adapt for real work.
prereqs: Wired headphones, not speakers — on speakers the avatar talks to itself.
A Deepgram API key from console.deepgram.com. New accounts get credit, no card needed.
A SpatialReal API key and App ID from app.spatialreal.ai (Apps → Create API Key). The free tier covers the workshop.
For the Pipecat build: an Anthropic API key, and uv (it installs Python for you).
artifact: A Pipecat avatar bot on the attendee’s own laptop that can be switched to a front-desk assistant, tutor or any other character.

slides.title: The Voice AI Economy is Powered by Deepgram
Give your voice agent a face
bullets: Links for the room: dpgr.am/gwt-links
slides.note: The room joins guest wifi here. The password is given out loud, not published — this page is readable without an event code.

slides.title: Why put a face on a voice agent?
bullets: People look at faces: a screen with a face gets attention a waveform does not
Seeing lips move helps people follow speech in a loud room
A face sets the tone — calm for a clinic, upbeat for a store
It makes a screen feel staffed when nobody is free
slides.note: The face is not the intelligence. The listening, thinking and speaking are the same voice agent; the avatar is how it shows up on a screen.

slides.title: Where avatars earn their keep
bullets: Front desks and kiosks: hotels, clinic check-in, offices, event booths
Training and role-play: sales calls, job interviews, hard conversations
Tutoring and language practice
Support on a website or in an app
Internal help desks: HR, IT, new-hire onboarding
slides.note: Ask the room which one their company could use. The common thread: a person would otherwise be standing at a screen, waiting or repeating the same answers.

slides.title: When to skip the face
bullets: Phone calls — there is no screen, so use a plain voice agent
When every fraction of a second or cent matters
When people need to read, not watch: forms, code, long numbers
When a human must answer: diagnoses, legal or money decisions
slides.note: Same pipeline either way. Removing the avatar is deleting one line, which is the point of Pipecat.

slides.title: What you need
bullets: A laptop with Chrome, and wired headphones (not speakers)
A Deepgram key — console.deepgram.com
A SpatialReal API key + App ID — app.spatialreal.ai → Apps
To build it yourself: an Anthropic key, plus uv (docs.astral.sh/uv)
slides.note: Everyone tries the avatar in the browser first. The Pipecat build is the main event and most people can do it; anyone who would rather not install anything stays in the browser.

slides.title: Over to SpatialReal
bullets: What SpatialReal is and who uses it
How the face is made and lip-synced
Pricing, and how to start for free
Questions
slides.note: The SpatialReal team presents here with their own slides: the product and pricing. Then we build the same avatar with Pipecat.

slides.title: Pipecat in one sentence
bullets: An open-source Python framework for real-time voice and video agents
You list the steps; Pipecat handles streaming, turn-taking and interruptions
Built by Daily, now part of Deepgram
docs.pipecat.ai
slides.note: Without a framework, a voice agent is a tangle of sockets, audio buffers and timers. Pipecat turns it into a list.

slides.title: Frames flow through processors
bullets: Everything is a frame: a slice of audio, a transcript, a word from the LLM, “user started speaking”
A processor takes frames in and pushes frames out
A pipeline is processors in order
A transport moves audio between the pipeline and the browser (or a phone line)
slides.note: Four words to remember: frame, processor, pipeline, transport. Everything else is detail.

slides.title: Our pipeline, top to bottom
bullets: transport.input() — your microphone arrives
stt — Deepgram Flux turns speech into text and hears when you finish
user_aggregator — adds what you said to the conversation
llm — Claude writes the reply, in character
tts — Deepgram Flux speaks it (voice: Brooke)
avatar — SpatialReal animates the face to that speech
transport.output() — sound and animation go to your browser
assistant_aggregator — remembers what was actually said
slides.note: Read it like a recipe. This is the real Pipeline([...]) list in bot.py.

slides.title: Every box is swappable
bullets: stt = DeepgramFluxSTTService(...)
llm = AnthropicLLMService(...)
tts = DeepgramFluxTTSService(...)
avatar = SpatialRealAvatarProcessor(...)
Change one line, and the rest keeps working
slides.note: Pipecat has dozens of services. A different LLM, voice or face is a different class on one line.

slides.title: How the face plugs in
bullets: The avatar processor sits right after the TTS
It reads the speech audio and sends animation to the browser, lined up with the sound
In the browser, SpatialReal’s SDK draws the face
The browser gets a short-lived token, never your API key
slides.note: SpatialReal shipped this processor as pipecat-spatialreal, and it is in the official Pipecat docs.

slides.title: Three commands
bullets: cp env.example .env   (then paste your keys)
uv sync
uv run bot.py -t webrtc
Open localhost:7860/avatar/ and press Start
slides.note: The walkthrough below goes step by step, with a check after each one.

slides.title: Same face, new job
bullets: CHARACTER=front-desk in .env
BUSINESS_NAME and BUSINESS_FACTS: who it works for and what it knows
Restart the bot — same face, new job
A new character is a new file in prompts/, not new code
slides.note: This is the move that turns a workshop demo into something useful on Monday.

slides.title: After today
bullets: No install: this page works any time with your own keys
Your own build: github.com/saccoface/pipecat-avatar-starter
Put it online: Pipecat Cloud hosts Pipecat bots
On the phone: Pipecat has telephony transports (no face needed)
slides.note: Everything runs on the attendee’s own keys, so there is nothing to hand back after the event.

slides.title: Keep going
bullets: docs.pipecat.ai — guides and every service
docs.pipecat.ai → Video → SpatialReal
app.spatialreal.ai/avatars/library — more faces
slides.note: Thank the room, and point at the starter repo one more time.

flow.title: Sit down and try it
flow.note: Nothing to install. Paste your SpatialReal and Deepgram keys, pick a face and press Start. The avatar interviews you for a couple of minutes, so you get a feel for how it looks, sounds and keeps up, and whether you would use one. Your answers, without names, join the room totals at the top of the page.

flow.title: Build it with Pipecat
flow.note: Follow along on your own laptop. Each step ends with a check, so you know it worked before moving on.

sections.title: Build it with Pipecat
sections.summary: The avatar you just tried, running as your own Pipecat bot on your laptop: Deepgram Flux listens and speaks, Claude thinks, SpatialReal draws the face. About 20 minutes, most of it sign-ups.

steps.title: Install uv
steps.instruction: uv installs Python and the project’s packages in one go. Mac: run curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh in Terminal. Windows: follow docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation. Then close and reopen the terminal.
steps.check: uv --version prints a version number.

steps.title: Download the starter
steps.instruction: On github.com/saccoface/pipecat-avatar-starter click the green Code button, then Download ZIP. Unzip it to your Desktop, and in the terminal run cd ~/Desktop/pipecat-avatar-starter.
steps.check: The folder holds bot.py, a client folder, a prompts folder and env.example.

steps.title: Collect four keys
steps.instruction: Deepgram: console.deepgram.com → API Keys → Create a New API Key. Anthropic: console.anthropic.com → API Keys → Create Key. SpatialReal: app.spatialreal.ai → Apps → Create API Key, and copy both the API key and the App ID (it starts with app_).
steps.check: You have a Deepgram key, an Anthropic key, a SpatialReal key and an App ID. Each key is shown once — if you lose one, make another.

steps.title: Pick a face
steps.instruction: Open app.spatialreal.ai/avatars/library, hover an avatar you like and click its copy icon. Vivian is f37f5990-4ee1-4add-8136-df9940f85567.
steps.check: You have an avatar ID — a long string of letters, numbers and dashes.

steps.title: Fill in .env
steps.instruction: Run cp env.example .env, open .env in any text editor and paste DEEPGRAM_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, SPATIALREAL_API_KEY, SPATIALREAL_APP_ID and SPATIALREAL_AVATAR_ID.
steps.check: Every line you filled has a value right after the = sign, with no spaces or quotes. .env stays on your laptop; it is never uploaded.

steps.title: Start the bot
steps.instruction: Run uv sync (about a minute the first time), then uv run bot.py -t webrtc. Leave this terminal open — the bot runs only while it stays open.
steps.check: The terminal ends with the bot listening on localhost:7860. If it names a missing setting, fix that line in .env and run it again.

steps.title: Talk to it
steps.instruction: Headphones on. Open http://localhost:7860/avatar/ in Chrome, allow the microphone and press Start.
steps.check: The face loads, greets you and asks how the night is going, and answers when you speak. Talk over it: it stops and listens.

sections.title: Read the code: a guided tour of bot.py
sections.summary: Seven short stops through the file, so you understand what each part does and could build the next one yourself.

steps.title: The four services
steps.instruction: Open bot.py and scroll to run_bot(). Find the numbered comments 1 to 4: Ears (DeepgramFluxSTTService), Brain (AnthropicLLMService), Voice (DeepgramFluxTTSService) and Face (SpatialRealAvatarProcessor). Each is one object, made with a key and a few settings.
steps.check: You can point at the line that picks the voice (DEEPGRAM_VOICE, default flux-brooke-en) and the line that picks the model (CLAUDE_MODEL near the top).

steps.title: Ears: Flux knows when you have finished
steps.instruction: DeepgramFluxSTTService streams your audio to Deepgram Flux. Flux returns the words and also decides when your turn is over, so there is no separate silence detector to tune. That end-of-turn signal is what lets the avatar answer quickly and stop when you interrupt.
steps.check: Pause mid-sentence for a second and keep going. The avatar should wait rather than jump in.

steps.title: Brain: the prompt is the character
steps.instruction: AnthropicLLMService sends the conversation to Claude. Its system_instruction is the text of prompts/host-interview.md. CLAUDE_MODEL is claude-haiku-4-5, chosen because it starts talking fastest (about 0.7 seconds in our tests).
steps.check: Open prompts/host-interview.md and find the seven questions it asks and the rules it follows.

steps.title: The pipeline is the order things happen
steps.instruction: Find Pipeline([...]). Read it top to bottom: transport.input(), stt, user_aggregator, llm, tts, avatar, transport.output(), assistant_aggregator. Frames flow down this list. The avatar comes after tts because it needs the speech audio to animate the face.
steps.check: You can say in one sentence why the avatar is not before tts.

steps.title: Memory: the two aggregators
steps.instruction: LLMContextAggregatorPair makes two processors that share one LLMContext. user_aggregator adds what you said; assistant_aggregator, placed after the output, adds what the bot actually spoke. If you interrupt, only the words that were spoken are remembered.
steps.check: Ask the avatar what you asked it first. It remembers, because of the context.

steps.title: Worker, runner and events
steps.instruction: PipelineWorker runs the pipeline for one conversation; WorkerRunner keeps it going until the browser disconnects. Event handlers react to moments: on_client_ready makes the avatar greet you first, on_client_disconnected shuts the session down.
steps.check: Find greet() and change its message, restart, and hear a different opening.

steps.title: Why the key never reaches the browser
steps.instruction: The /spatialreal-token route uses your SpatialReal key on the server to get a token that expires in an hour, and gives the browser only that. It also refuses requests from other websites, so a random page cannot spend your credits.
steps.check: Open http://localhost:7860/spatialreal-token in a tab: you see a token, not your API key.

sections.title: Make it yours
sections.summary: Change the voice, the face and the job — each is one line in .env or one text file. This is how you use it after today.

steps.title: Change the voice
steps.instruction: In .env set DEEPGRAM_VOICE to another Flux voice — flux-kit-en, flux-cole-en, flux-hannah-en and dozens more are listed at developers.deepgram.com/docs/flux-tts/voices. Restart the bot (Ctrl+C, then uv run bot.py -t webrtc) and refresh the page.
steps.check: The same face speaks with the new voice and still lip-syncs. One line changed.

steps.title: Change the face
steps.instruction: Copy another avatar ID from app.spatialreal.ai/avatars/library into SPATIALREAL_AVATAR_ID, restart and refresh.
steps.check: A different person appears, with the same voice and character.

steps.title: Give it a real job
steps.instruction: In .env set CHARACTER=front-desk, BUSINESS_NAME to a business (your own, or a made-up café) and BUSINESS_FACTS to a few plain sentences: hours, address, what you sell, who to ask for help. Restart and refresh.
steps.check: The avatar greets you as that business’s assistant, answers from your facts, and says it is not sure when you ask something the facts do not cover.

steps.title: Write your own character
steps.instruction: Copy prompts/front-desk.md to a new file, say prompts/tutor.md, and rewrite it. Any [UPPER_CASE] word in brackets is filled from .env, so [SUBJECT] reads SUBJECT=. Set CHARACTER=tutor and restart.
steps.check: Your character runs without touching bot.py. If a placeholder is missing from .env, the terminal names it.

steps.title: Use it with no install
steps.instruction: Anyone on your team can use the version at the top of this page any time: paste their own Deepgram and SpatialReal keys, pick a face and talk. Nothing is stored on this site.
steps.check: A teammate gets it running in under five minutes with only a browser.

steps.title: Take it further
steps.instruction: To put your bot online for others, Pipecat Cloud hosts Pipecat bots — start at docs.pipecat.ai. To answer phone calls instead, Pipecat has telephony transports for providers such as Twilio; drop the avatar line, since phones have no screen.
steps.check: You know which path fits your idea: browser, hosted, or phone.

troubleshooting: The avatar talks to itself: you are on speakers. Switch to wired headphones.
The avatar appears for a second, then vanishes: the free SpatialReal tier allows 2 sessions at once. Close other tabs running an avatar and press Start again.
SpatialReal needs both an API key and an App ID, and the App ID starts with app_. They sit side by side on the Apps page.
A key is rejected: copy it again, whole, with no spaces. A Deepgram key is 40 letters and numbers, not the dashed key ID shown in the list.
Pipecat: the terminal says a setting is not set — that line in .env is empty or misspelled. Fix it and restart the bot.
Pipecat: CHARACTER=… has no prompts/….md — the name must match a file in prompts/, without .md.
Pipecat: port 7860 is in use — run uv run bot.py -t webrtc --port 7861, open that port, and change PIPECAT_ALLOWED_ORIGINS in .env to match.
Sessions stop after 10 minutes on the free SpatialReal tier. Press Start again.
